sections.heading: Overview

sections.content:
Design and Construct – Milton Ulladulla bypass (MUb)
The Milton Ulladulla bypass is located within the Shoalhaven Local Government Area (LGA) and will provide a critical upgrade to the Princes Highway on the NSW South Coast.
The project will improve safety and travel reliability by bypassing the Milton and Ulladulla town centres, reducing congestion, supporting more efficient freight and tourism movements, and enhancing connectivity for local communities and regional traffic.
The bypass will also improve network resilience and help separate local and through traffic, creating more liveable town centres and safer transport outcomes for all road users. Additional information is available at the Transport website: Milton Ulladulla bypass
sections.heading: Project goals

sections.content:
The successful tenderer will be selected through a two-phase procurement process. The first phase requires applicants to submit an EOI in response to the EOI documents. A shortlist of applicants will then be selected from this EOI process and invited to tender for the project.
The EOI documents and further details related to the EOI process are available only via the project data room. To gain access to the project data room for the EOI stage, prospective applicants will need to complete, sign and return the corporate confidentiality deed (in accordance with the instructions in that deed) and the initial data room representatives form (Annexure 1 to that deed) to: MUB_procurement@transport.nsw.gov.au
Following receipt of these duly executed documents, access to the EOI documents will be granted. The project data room is expected to be available for access from 21 September 2026.
An EOI briefing will be held via MS Teams during the first week following the release of the EOI. Attendance is not mandatory to submit a conforming Application.
Transport is considering the payment of bid cost contributions. Payment of any bid cost contribution is not guaranteed, and is subject to the relevant approvals, submissions providing innovative approaches to construction, providing better ‘value for money’ solutions to Transport, including NSW Treasury.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.content:
Applicants must comply with the Transport Statement of Business Ethics through the procurement process and any subsequent contract period.
Applicants must comply with the NSW Government Procurement Policy Framework, NSW Government Supplier Code of Conduct and New South Wales Industrial Relations Guidelines: Building and Construction Procurement.
The MUB will be jointly funded by the Australian and NSW Governments.
It is a requirement for the project that the successful contractor be accredited under the Australian Government Work Health and Safety Accreditation Scheme (the Scheme) at the time of entering into the contract for ‘building work’ for the project and must maintain accreditation under the Scheme while the ‘building work’ is being carried out. Information on the Scheme is available on the Australian Government website at fsc.gov.au.
